title: Chicken Little
summary:
Chicken Little
With the contraction of the global economy, the question on the minds of many is how it will affect the tanker market in the immediate term. Although tankers is still one of the most viable shipping sectors, the last few months have seen asset prices soften, newbuilding orders cease and freight rates return to long-term averages. In attempts to answer the question, we turn our attention to the physical crude tanker market to see what happened so far this year.

children.title: All's Quiet on the Waterfront
children.summary: The map below suggests generally less supply from the Arabian Gulf (AG), which saw a total decrease in spot fixture volume from October 2008 through January 2009 as compared to the previous year. VLCCs bore the weight of the decrease with a 67 fixture drop.

children.title: Month-on-Month
children.summary: While most signs point to a slowdown, it should be noted that December 2008 alone saw increased activity versus December 2007. VLCCs, Suezmaxes and Aframaxes saw gains of 65, 70 and 75 reported spot fixtures respectively on last year's December totals.
